champion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy
ordered_diagnoses: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of jaundice, weight loss, abdominal pain, and muscle weakness with elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin
salient_findings: Mild weakness in bilateral hip flexor muscles
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase) and bilirubin
key_facts: 71-year-old man presented with three weeks of jaundice
Weight loss and abdominal pain reported
Bilateral lower-extremity weakness, most noticeable when arising from a chair
No history of autoimmune or neuromuscular conditions
Taking atorvastatin as a home medication
Epigastric tenderness without guarding or rebound on physical examination
Significant elevation in creatinine kinase (CK) level
CT abdomen/pelvis showed a 2.6 × 3.1 cm pancreatic head mass
MRI showed diffuse myositis affecting lower extremities
Pancreatic head biopsy was hypocellular with scant atypical cells
Biliary stricture biopsy was consistent with adenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pancreatic head mass with associated pancreatic ductal dilatation and biliary stricture biopsy consistent with adenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Significant elevation in creatinine kinase (CK) level and myopathic changes consistent with rhabdomyolysis on right biceps femoris biopsy

shortlist.label: Statins-induced myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was taking atorvastatin as a home medication, which can cause myopathy

shortlist.label: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Pancreatic head mass and diffuse myositis affecting lower extremities, suggesting a paraneoplastic syndrome

shortlist.label: Cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Biliary stricture biopsy consistent with adenocarcinoma and significant elevation in cancer antigen 19-9 level, which can be associated with cholangiocarcinoma

s4.champion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy

raw.champion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with jaundice, weight loss, abdominal pain, and a pancreatic head mass on CT, along with the biopsy results showing adenocarcinoma, supports the diagnosis of pancreatic cancer. The significant elevation in creatinine kinase level and the MRI findings of diffuse myositis affecting lower extremities, in the context of a new diagnosis of pancreatic cancer, suggest a paraneoplastic syndrome, specifically paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy.

rejected.label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has pancreatic adenocarcinoma, this diagnosis alone does not explain the muscle weakness and elevated CK levels.

rejected.label: Rhabdomyolysis
rejected.why: Rhabdomyolysis is a possible complication but does not explain the underlying cause of the patient's symptoms and the pancreatic mass.

rejected.label: Statins-induced myopathy
rejected.why: Although the patient is taking atorvastatin, the presence of a pancreatic mass and the biopsy results indicating adenocarcinoma suggest a paraneoplastic syndrome rather than a statin-induced myopathy.

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results and imaging studies specifically point towards pancreatic adenocarcinoma rather than cholangiocarcinoma.
